messages:
Charlie: Hey support — running into a production SSO issue. GitHub login is failing at our callback with a 403 and the logs say "state mismatch". Happens intermittently behind our CDN/proxy. Repro: click login -> redirect -> 403. Example callback payload looks like duplicate state in the URL. Any ideas?

Sasha (Support): Thanks @Charlie — can you paste the exact callback URL from a failed session and which proxies are in front of the app (CloudFront/NGINX/other)?

Charlie: Sure — here's a redacted example from a failing request we captured:
`https://auth.redwood-app.com/callback?code=gho_ABC123...&state=abc123&state=abc123&client_id=acme&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Facme.app%2Fauth%2Fcb`
We have CloudFront -> nginx (ELB) -> app. We suspect the CDN or our rewrite is duplicating the param.

Priya (Eng Backend): Duplicate `state` param explains it. Our validator expects exactly one `state` param; if there are multiple values we reject (safety). Can you paste any proxy rewrite rules or the raw request headers/nginx logs?

Charlie: Attaching minimal nginx snippet (redacted):
```
server {
  listen 443;
  location / {
    proxy_pass http://upstream;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
  }
}
```
And an access log line: `GET /callback?code=gho_ABC123&state=abc123&state=abc123 HTTP/1.1" 403 12 "-" "Mozilla/5.0"`
Also saw `cf-forwarded-query: state=abc123; state=abc123` in our logs.

Sasha (Support): OK can you run a raw curl from inside your infra to our callback so we can see exactly how it arrives at our edge? Example: `curl -v "https://auth.redwood-app.com/callback?code=test&state=abc123&state=abc123"` — paste the verbose response.

Charlie: Ran it and attached the verbose output. Interestingly the request arrives at your edge with both `state` values; but when our nginx forwards upstream sometimes it collapses into one. Seems ordering and duplication behavior differs across layers.

Priya (Eng Backend): Noted — CloudFront and some proxies canonicalize query strings differently. Two plausible approaches: 1) make our callback tolerant to duplicate `state` params if values are identical (safer short-term), or 2) require upstream to ensure single param. We'll push a small validator change to accept identical duplicate values and log a diagnostic field with raw query string for triage.

Sasha (Support): Quick workaround for you: if you can change the redirect to include `state` as a fragment (e.g., `#state=...`) the server won't see it, but fragments are client-side only — so only do that if your flow supports client-side exchange. Alternatively, ensure the CDN doesn't have any query-string normalization policy that merges/duplicates keys.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T22:01:00 started: patch/auth-callback-dup-state-tolerant

Priya (Eng Backend): We pushed a canary that tolerates duplicate `state` when all values are identical and emits a new debug header `x-auth-raw-query` with the raw query string (redacted in logs). Canary set to 10% now. Will monitor metrics for malformed states.

Sasha (Support): @Charlie once canary is live can you try a login and paste the browser network trace (Request URL and response code)? That will help confirm the fix. Thanks!

Charlie: Tried after ~8 minutes — our previously failing tenants can now complete login, 403s stopped. Browser network trace shows `200` on callback and the app exchanges code. Everything seems green. Thanks all! :tada:

Priya (Eng Backend): Great — we will merge the tolerance patch to main and follow up with a proper fix: ENG-4921 to add unit tests for duplicate-query handling and update docs about intermediaries normalizing queries.

Sasha (Support): Closing the ticket as resolved for now. If you see recurrence please re-open and include the `x-auth-raw-query` value from logs. :thumbsup:
